paper.title_en: Algebraic versus physical uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators
paper.abstract_en: We give explicit determinant counterexamples to the uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators from their degrees and simultaneous pair zeros. At seven points the solution space has dimension seven; Bose symmetry removes six directions and leaves the Hodges line. At eight points a two-dimensional Bose-symmetric space remains. Regular integer-spinor configurations distinguish these deformations from the Hodges numerator. On the eight-point plane, collinear factorization, the leading positive-helicity soft coefficient and ordinary BCFW decay each select the Hodges line. For $n\ge5$, we prove two results on the full fixed-degree, common-denominator ansatz, without pair-zero conditions. Complete collinear residue functions on all pairs determine at most one numerator; Bose symmetry makes one channel sufficient. The splitting law and a normalized lower-point amplitude supply the boundary function, starting from an explicit five-point seed. With Bose symmetry, $O(Z^{-1})$ decay under one fixed same-helicity shift at generic conserving kinematics also selects the Hodges line. Normalized collinear and soft data fix the eight-point scale; the homogeneous shift condition leaves one constant per multiplicity.
